title: GitHub Trending Summary - Daily - 2026-11-25
ranking_basis: GitHub Trending daily star gains, ordered by the supplied candidate score; score components and 30-day Trending days used as supporting signals.
ranking_explanation: Selected the ten highest-scoring supplied candidates. The score components show normalized period gain plus 0.5 times days_trending_30d. All ten selected candidates had five Trending days in the last 30 days; the score order also follows their daily star-gain order.
global_caveat: Historical star-snapshot deltas are null because the signal run could not authenticate gh CLI. Live REST star totals can differ slightly from the signal file's totals-at-collection. One-day Trending gains indicate current attention, not durable adoption.

sources.corroboration: GitHub Search API exact repository searches plus public REST repository and default-branch commit endpoints; all ten had exact search matches and current commits.
sources.snapshot_source_status: error: gh CLI was unauthenticated; delta_1d, delta_7d, and delta_30d unavailable
sources.deepwiki: Not used; first-party README content was available for the five highest-ranked repositories.

sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Daily snapshot for 2026-11-25, 03:21 UTC. Daily Trending star gains, ordered by supplied candidate score with available 30-day Trending days as supporting evidence.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: The strongest signal is a wave of agent-oriented developer tooling: security skills, reusable coding-agent workflows, and CLIs that make existing software usable by agents. The ten leading supplied candidates gained 703–1,826 stars in today's Trending view; each had appeared on Trending on five days in the last 30 days.

sections.title: elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter
sections.description: A Claude Code bundle for authorized bug hunting and red-team work, organized as skills, commands, vulnerability patterns, and reporting workflows.
sections.why_notable: Highest supplied candidate score (10.010), daily gain, and Trending rank (#1); its README describes a layered workflow spanning methodology, web-app hunting, enterprise attack chains, and evidence/reporting.
sections.unique_caveat: Security testing workflows should only be used within authorized scope.

enrichment.architecture_summary: A Claude Code skills/plugin bundle with optional CLI and engagement scaffolding, organized into methodology, web-app hunting, enterprise attack-chain, and reporting/evidence layers.
enrichment.workflow: Install as a plugin or copy the bundle; describe an in-scope target in plain language; relevant skills load to guide reconnaissance and testing; triage and evidence/reporting workflows follow.
enrichment.design_pattern: Topic-triggered specialist skills composed into an explicit, scope-aware security workflow.

sections.title: XiaoYouChR/Ghost-Downloader-3
sections.description: A cross-platform desktop downloader covering common web, streaming, peer-to-peer, and file-hosting sources.
sections.why_notable: Second-highest supplied score (9.497) and a broad, integrated download workflow across Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android.

enrichment.architecture_summary: A cross-platform desktop application paired with a browser extension and plugin-style Feature Packs; the README describes support for Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android.
enrichment.workflow: Select or detect downloadable media in the app or browser extension, configure quality or headers as needed, then manage the transfer in the desktop client; downloads can be controlled through the RPC API.
enrichment.design_pattern: One multi-protocol client with browser handoff and extensible feature packs.

sections.title: HKUDS/CLI-Anything
sections.description: A toolkit and community registry for creating command-line harnesses that let AI agents operate existing software.
sections.why_notable: Score 9.480 and daily Trending rank #3; its README emphasizes generated software-specific CLIs plus a hub for browsing and installing community harnesses.

enrichment.architecture_summary: A Python-based harness-generation project that exposes software through agent-friendly CLIs, complemented by a community registry and installer hub.
enrichment.workflow: Install the hub, browse and install a harness, then let a compatible coding agent invoke the target software through the generated CLI; contributors can submit additional harnesses.
enrichment.design_pattern: A standardized CLI adapter layer turns existing applications into callable agent tools, with a shared community catalog.

sections.title: obra/superpowers
sections.description: A cross-agent software-development methodology packaged as composable skills and instructions.
sections.why_notable: Score 9.412 and daily Trending rank #2; its documented flow moves from clarifying a spec and reviewing a design to planned, test-driven, subagent-led implementation.

enrichment.architecture_summary: Composable skills and initial instructions guide coding agents through a repeatable development methodology and are packaged for multiple agent harnesses.
enrichment.workflow: Clarify requirements into a spec, present and approve a design, create an implementation plan, then execute tasks with true red/green TDD and agent review.
enrichment.design_pattern: A staged, skill-triggered development process that imposes review gates before implementation and delegates planned tasks to subagents.

sections.title: firecrawl/firecrawl
sections.description: Web search, scraping, crawling, and data access tools aimed at agent knowledge workflows.
sections.why_notable: Score 9.400 and daily Trending rank #6; the README distinguishes a local binary/MCP/API path, a hosted service, and a self-hosted server.

enrichment.architecture_summary: The repository contains Firecrawl Local, a self-hosted server, and SDKs; hosted cloud offers additional scale, search, and data-provider access.
enrichment.workflow: Run local scrape, crawl, or map commands or connect an agent through MCP; use the localhost API for compatible SDKs; move to cloud or self-hosted deployment for larger workloads and additional services.
enrichment.design_pattern: A local-first interface with compatible API and MCP surfaces, plus hosted and self-hosted deployment modes.

sections.title: zhouxiaoka/autoclip
sections.description: An open-source AI video-clipping and content-repurposing desktop tool for turning long recordings into short-form media.
sections.why_notable: Score 9.389, daily Trending rank #16; the repository page describes automated subtitles, covers, and publishing copy for major short-video platforms.

sections.title: mjmirza/app-store-compliance
sections.description: A pre-submission playbook and guard for App Store and Google Play requirements.
sections.why_notable: Score 9.334 and daily Trending rank #12; its listing combines rejection-pattern guidance, privacy checks, regulatory deadlines, and coding-agent support.

sections.title: cathrynlavery/diagram-design
sections.description: A diagram-design toolkit for coding agents, with 52 diagram types built from self-contained HTML and SVG.
sections.why_notable: Score 9.188 and daily Trending rank #9; it represents a design-tooling strand alongside the more numerous agent workflow and infrastructure projects.

sections.title: jingyaogong/minimind
sections.description: A compact, from-scratch language-model training project with a documented end-to-end training path.
sections.why_notable: Score 9.090 and daily Trending rank #4; its README describes a small model intended to make training and experimentation feasible on modest personal hardware.

sections.title: mvanhorn/last30days-skill
sections.description: An agent skill that researches a topic across social, video, forum, prediction-market, and web sources.
sections.why_notable: Score 9.057 and daily Trending rank #10; it extends the agent-skill pattern from coding into multi-source research and grounded synthesis.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent tooling dominates the shared pattern: CLI-Anything makes applications agent-callable, while Superpowers and Claude-BugHunter package workflows as composable skills; last30days-skill applies that pattern to research. Firecrawl and last30days-skill point to demand for agent knowledge access. Consumer utility momentum also appears in Ghost-Downloader-3 and AutoClip. Languages among the selected ten: Python 6, Shell 2, TypeScript 1, HTML 1.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's list is led by tooling that makes agents more capable through reusable workflows, software interfaces, and access to external knowledge—not by a single model release. The set also has substantial non-agent utility momentum, especially in downloading and video repurposing. These gains are a one-day Trending signal, not evidence by themselves of long-term adoption; historical star-delta snapshots were unavailable for this run.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary: GitHub Trending daily and the supplied signal file. Corroboration: exact GitHub Search API matches and public REST repository/default-branch commit endpoints for all ten. Star gains, daily ranks, candidate scores, and Trending-day counts are from the signal file; live current total stars and default-branch commit SHAs are from REST. Snapshot deltas were unavailable because gh CLI lacked authentication. No prior-window comparison is claimed.
